thread:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on continuous-batch serving path in us-west-2. SLO (p99 < 300ms) breached for ~4m. Paging oncall (rotation: Eve) :rotating_light:
Eve: I'm on it. initial check: dashboard shows p95 ~180ms, p99 ~620ms, error rate stable. streaming stalls increasing, tail tokens show long KV fetchs.
Sam: adding context — we pushed batching scheduler change 2h ago that tweaked fairness weights; could be interaction with mixed seqlen workload.
Maya: pulling traces now. initial flame shows long wait time in batch-queue, not GPU exec. looks like preemption+padding amplification.
Eve: assigning triage. Sam/Maya/Lucas please coordinate. customer-impact: a few high-throughput chat customers seeing degraded streaming latency. no increase in 5xxs.
Lucas: running a quick histogram: batch sizes spiked median->90th ~ 3x for mixedlen requests; preempt evictions up. also KV-cache miss rate ticked up.
Ryan: can we temporarily route streaming traffic to the dedicated pool for affected customers? policy exists.
Sam: yes we can. making route change for tag:customer-legacy-chat to dedicated-usw2-d. doing canary (1% -> 10%).
Eve: good. Maya, any mitigations on scheduler?
Maya: we can flip scheduler back to previous fairness weights and reduce max_batch_size from 512 -> 256. both are hot config flips. but changing weights requires restart of batcher processes (graceful).
Eve: What's risk of restart?
Maya: short term: some active batches may be requeued, could cause small blips <30s. overall should reduce padding amplification.
Lucas: also recommending enabling kv-prefetch heuristic for streaming path (low-risk config).
Ryan: I can do route shift + kv-prefetch toggle. Sam can prepare rollback.
Sam: prepared rollback steps in runbook: /runbooks/contbatch-tail-mitigation (link) — will revert routing and reapply original scheduler weights.
oncall-bot: Deploy bot: starting config update: reduce max_batch_size -> 256 in batcher group prod-usw2. Change request id: CR-8921.
Eve: rolling. keep all comms here. Sam, watch p99, Lucas watch queue depths, Maya watch preemption counts.
Maya: FYI logs: see repeated lines in batcher logs like: `wait_for_batch timeout=1200ms requeue=true padding=320` — suggests padding amplification due to head-of-line long sequences.
Lucas: live metric: preemption_count dropped 60% after initial KV-prefetch toggle (just flipped). p99 dipped from 620ms -> 410ms.
Sam: routing to dedicated for 10% completed. those customers show p99 ~ 220ms now.
Eve: good. continue gradual ramp to 50% over next 5 mins.
Ryan: ramp to 50% done. systemwide p99 now 350ms. still above SLO but much improved.
Maya: starting batcher restart schedule to apply fairness rollback (staggered across nodes every 30s). doing safe drain.
Sam: restarting node pool batcher-1a now.
Eve: any downstream impact to non-streaming (inference/generate) paths?
Maya: no exec latency change; this is queueing.
Lucas: after two restarts p99 at 280ms. p95 at 150ms. preemption evictions normalized.
Eve: can we mark incident as mitigated if p99 stays < 320ms for 10m?
Sam: agree. still keep route to dedicated for high-throughput customers until next maintenance window.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Sev2 -> Mitigated. Trigger: p99 recovered to 285ms across regions. 
Eve: documenting postmortem items inline: 1) rollback fairness weights caused mixed-seqlen amplification; need automated canary for batch-size distribution. 2) add per-customer routing auto-fallback if p99 > threshold. 3) need KV-prefetch on by default for streaming path. 4) add alert for batch padding growth metric.
Maya: will open a ticket for quantifying padding amplification and implement histogram-based auto-shed for very long sequences.
Lucas: I'll schedule a follow-up to tune default max_batch_size per model family.
Sam: updating runbook with exact mitigation steps we used (routing, kv-prefetch, weight rollback). link -> https://redwood.runbooks/contbatch-tail-8921
Eve: handing off to next oncall (Ryan) for monitoring and postmortem writeup. Ryan, you're up.
Ryan: taking handoff. I'll run 1hr watch and start the postmortem draft.
Eve: thanks team. closing page. :white_check_mark:
